title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-tess-wong
content:
Context:
- Repro intermittent OOMs on dedicated cluster (dedicated-pool-03) when running large-batch inference (batch_size=8, seq_len=4096) on A100-40GB nodes. Seen across a few model variants (rwkv-large, llama-13b-q4f16) after recent system upgrades.

Observed symptoms / error snippets:
- Typical PyTorch OOM:
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 5.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 31.20 GiB already allocated; 3.12 GiB free; 32.84 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  Note: allocation fails even though nvidia-smi shows ~6GB free (fragmentation suspected).

- Occasionally see driver/library mismatch (after reboot of node):
  E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:318] failed call to cuInit: CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE -- which is wrong, GPU present
  PyTorch warning: Found GPU driver that does not support all features required by CUDA runtime version 11.8
  RuntimeError: CUDA error: initialization error (cuInit fails)

- Rare cuBLAS init failure on some container restarts:
  CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling `cublasCreate(handle)`

- dmesg excerpts (from node dedicated-pool-03-07):
  [Mar  1 02:11:47 kernel] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:3B:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [Mar  1 02:11:48 kernel] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3B:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
  (these lines correlate with the time of a model rollout + heavy batching)

Environment (notes captured during repro):
- GPU: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (driver reported by nvidia-smi: 535.54.03)
- CUDA: host has 11.8 installed; container base image uses cuda:11.7 from nvidia/cuda
- PyTorch: 2.2.0+cu118 (but some containers pinned to cu117 builds)
- Container runtime: containerd on Ubuntu 22.04, NVIDIA Container Toolkit 1.12
- Orchestration: Kubernetes v1.25, device-plugin + MIG not enabled for these nodes

Commands I ran (notes, outputs summarized):
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION (shows fragmentation pattern - many allocations small, some big unused chunks)
- docker run --gpus all --rm -it --entrypoint=bash nvidia/cuda:11.7-base \
    # inside: python -c \"import torch; print(torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available()); x=torch.zeros((1,1024,1024), device='cuda'); print(x.device)\"
  -> shows cuda available sometimes, other times cuInit fails inside container (mismatch suspected)
- ssh into node -> sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | grep -i nvrm -> saw 'GPU has fallen off the bus' lines
- checked loaded driver: modinfo nvidia | grep version -> 535.54.03
- checked container toolkit logs -> /var/log/nvidia-container-runtime.log (no obvious errors but some warnings about compatibility)
- torch.cuda.empty_cache() and del tensors between runs -> temporarily reduces OOM frequency but doesn't fix

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver / CUDA runtime mismatch across host vs container -> containers using cuda:11.7 while host driver is newer; some CUDA runtime features require matching toolkit/runtime. This explains sporadic cuInit failures after reboots/updates.
2) Memory fragmentation due to repeated allocations with mixed quantized kernels (q4f16) and non-quantized models; large sequence lengths cause many large KV-cache allocations leaving insufficient contiguous space.
3) Kernel/resident set instability from bad driver + heavy load causing GPU to 'fall off the bus' (Xid 79) -> hardware or driver bug triggered under sustained throughput.
4) Container runtime / cgroup limits or new containerd version interacting poorly with nvidia-container-toolkit patch -> rare allocation failures and incorrect visibility.

Things that helped (workarounds):
- Lowering batch_size from 8 -> 4 reduced OOM frequency dramatically on affected nodes.
- Using container image built with cuda:11.8 (matching host toolkit) removed the cuInit/no-device errors in my local repro.
- Pre-allocating KV cache / reusing buffers in serving runtime reduces fragmentation in long-run tests.
- Restarting node (after moving traffic) sometimes clears the 'fallen off the bus' state, but recurrence after heavy load.

Immediate next steps to validate root cause:
- Reproduce with controlled script that ramps batch size + seq_len in a loop, capture nvidia-smi snapshots every 10s, and dmesg output. Script: repro/gpu_oom_stress.py (I have a draft)
- Standardize container base to cuda:11.8 for all inference images (build/test) and roll to canary nodes.
- Run driver downgrade/upgrades on a staging node: try 535.86 -> 535.54 and also test 530 series (coordinate SRE).
- Enable MIG or limit per-container visible memory (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES + nvml quotas) to see if isolating reduces 'fall off the bus' events.
- Add kernel-level logging to detect Xid codes earlier and correlate with model events (rollouts).

Notes for SRE / infra handoff (what to include in ticket):
- Timestamps of incidents: 2026-02-28 22:10 UTC (OOM + Xid 79), 2026-02-28 22:15 UTC (node rebooted), 2026-03-01 01:04 UTC (cuInit errors after kubelet restart).
- Node IDs: dedicated-pool-03-07 (ip: 10.2.47.112), dedicated-pool-03-02 (less frequent).
- Container images observed: redwood/inference:prod-202602 - based on cuda:11.7 -> recommend rebuild on cuda:11.8
- Attach: nvidia-smi logs, dmesg snippets, container runtime logs, torch stack traces (compressed)

Longer-term thoughts / mitigation ideas:
- Move to more conservative default batch/seq configurations for canaries; gradual ramp-up with telemetry-based aborts when GPU error rates increase.
- Add a preflight check in runtime to validate container CUDA runtime vs host driver compatibility; warn/abort if mismatch detected.
- Evaluate using persistent buffer pooling in serving runtime to avoid fragmentation for long-lived workers.
- Make model rollout policy automatically reduce batch_size on nodes reporting increased Xid or cuBLAS allocation failures.

Unresolved questions:
- Are the Xid 79 events purely driver/hardware, or can bad kernels in our runtime trigger them? Need to reproduce under synthetic load.
- How tolerant is our current autoscaler to nodes that intermittently 'fall off the bus'? Traffic might be redirected slowly causing cascading failures.

Attachments / quick refs:
- Repro script path: /home/tess/repro/gpu_oom_stress.py (local draft)
- Temp logs: /tmp/tess/gpu-incident-20260228.tar.gz
- Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/487 (buffer pooling experiment)
- Jira: JIRA-INF-1023 (tracking driver mismatch + node instability)

Next actions (owned by me):
- [ ] Finalize repro script and run on isolated canary node (target: 2026-03-02)
- [ ] Rebuild inference image on cuda:11.8 and run smoke tests (target: 2026-03-03)
- [ ] Open SRE ticket with logs and request scheduled driver test (target: 2026-03-03)
- [ ] Try enabling MIG on one node to test isolation impact (depends on SRE)

Random notes and hypotheses I might forget if not written down:
- Sometimes mixing conda-installed cudatoolkit and system driver can present fine until a kernel update; the runtime only fails after specific sequence of operations (e.g., restart + heavy alloc).
- TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 sometimes helps fragmentation but can increase CPU overhead. Worth testing with long KV cache runs.

Timestamped edit log:
- 2026-02-20: initial notes during first repro attempts.
- 2026-02-28: added dmesg/Xid findings after incident.
- 2026-03-01: updated with container image mismatch hypothesis and next steps.
